strings.name: Kerry James Marshall
strings.summary: Kerry James Marshall is an American artist whose paintings center Black figures; he also works in sculpture and other media. Through portraiture, landscape and history painting, he explores Black life and its place in art history. Born in Birmingham and raised in Los Angeles, he later settled and worked in Chicago.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Exhibition records do not establish personal attendance; the Paris exhibition’s 2027 closing date remains scheduled. Honorary and earned degrees are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: His paintings reposition Black people within art history and everyday imagery, influencing American visual culture and museum narratives.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: BFA from Otis Art Institute in 1978; honorary doctorate from the same institution in 1999.
strings.facts.f2.label: Range of practice
strings.facts.f2.value: Known for painting, he also makes drawings, sculptures and installations; figures in his works do not all represent the artist himself.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Black figures and painting traditions
strings.highlights.h1.text: Places Black life at the center of large paintings, rethinking portraiture, landscape and history painting.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Exhibitions across institutions
strings.highlights.h2.text: Mastry and The Histories survey his work in separate exhibitions; the latter toured London, Zurich and Paris in 2025–2026.
strings.timeline.t1.title: The Histories in Paris
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Musée d’Art Moderne de Paris presents the exhibition, scheduled to run through January 24, 2027.
strings.timeline.t2.title: The Histories in Zurich
strings.timeline.t2.text: The Kunsthaus Zürich exhibition runs from February 27 to August 16.
strings.timeline.t3.title: The Histories in London
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Royal Academy of Arts exhibition opens, running through January 18, 2026.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Mastry in New York
strings.timeline.t4.text: The Met Breuer hosts the touring exhibition; the New York presentation runs through January 29, 2017.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Wolfgang Hahn Prize
strings.timeline.t5.text: The Gesellschaft für Moderne Kunst am Museum Ludwig awards the prize and acquires Vignette #15 for the museum.
strings.timeline.t6.title: MacArthur Fellowship
strings.timeline.t6.text: The MacArthur Foundation confirms his selection as a Fellow that year.
strings.timeline.t7.title: An early self-portrait painting
strings.timeline.t7.text: A Portrait of the Artist as a Shadow of His Former Self uses egg tempera on paper; it is a painting, not a photograph.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes a BFA
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduates from Otis Art Institute in Los Angeles; receives a separate honorary doctorate in 1999.
